Defining products

Source: vignettes/defining-products.Rmd
defining-products.Rmd

product() creates a specification row. products() combines rows and validates the resulting table. Lower priority values are considered first.

Product fields 

## Define a sawlog specification
saw <- product(product = 'saw',
               priority = 1,
               lengths = c(16, 32),
               trim = 0.5,
               min_sed = 6,
               volume_unit = 'scribner',
               inside_bark = TRUE)
product priority lengths trim min_sed volume_unit
saw 1 16, 32 0.5 6 scribner 
## Define a pulp specification
pulp <- product(product = 'pulp',
                priority = 2,
                min_length = 8,
                max_length = 20,
                length_step = 1,
                trim = 0.5,
                min_sed = 3,
                volume_unit = 'green_ton',
                accepts_pulp_restriction = TRUE)
## Combine and check the specifications
specifications <- products(saw, pulp) %>%
  validate_products()
product priority min_sed volume_unit accepts_pulp_restriction
saw 1 6 scribner FALSE
pulp 2 3 green_ton TRUE

Use lengths for discrete lengths or min_length, max_length, and length_step for a range. min_sed tests the physical small end, including trim. inside_bark chooses the diameter basis for acceptance.

Tree entry checks species, diameter, age, and pruning restrictions. allow_after_higher_product controls later use after an earlier product. allow_lower_products controls progression to subsequent products. Product fields control tree entry, log acceptance, and measurement.

## Select a shipped tree
tree <- example_trees %>%
  filter(tree == 5)
tree spcd species dbh ht model
5 202 Douglas-fir 20 100 F00FW2W202 
## Apply the specifications to the example tree
result <- merchandise(dbh = tree$dbh,
                      ht = tree$ht,
                      model = tree$model,
                      species = tree$species,
                      products = specifications,
                      status = TRUE)
log product nominal_length sed_ib net_scale scale_unit
1 saw 32 14.017 230.000 board_foot
2 saw 32 8.524 90.000 board_foot
3 pulp 20 3.474 0.102 green_short_ton

Shipped specifications

example_product_names() lists the available tables. example_products() loads one. product_presets() and product_preset() are compatibility names for the same operations.

## List the example tables
available <- example_product_names()
name status
pnw illustrative
us_south illustrative
douglas_fir illustrative 
## Load the example specifications
specifications <- example_products(name = 'pnw')
product lengths min_length max_length min_sed trim volume_unit
export 32, 40 NA NA 12 1.0 scribner
domestic_saw 16, 20, 24, 32, 40 NA NA 6 1.0 scribner
pulp 8 40 3 0.5 green_ton 
## Load the same specifications through the compatibility names
preset_names <- product_presets()

## Load a preset table
preset_products <- product_preset(name = 'pnw')
product priority volume_unit
export 1 scribner
domestic_saw 2 scribner
pulp 3 green_ton

Source rule records

nvel_rules() records National Volume Estimator Library settings. products_from_nvel_rules() translates a complete record into products and accompanying stem limits.

## Record the source segmentation and measurement settings
rules <- nvel_rules(even_or_odd = 2,
                    option = 14,
                    maximum_length = 40,
                    minimum_length = 8,
                    minimum_top_length = 8,
                    merchantable_length = 80,
                    primary_top = 6,
                    secondary_top = 4,
                    stump = 1,
                    trim = 0.5,
                    bark_ratio = 0.9,
                    minimum_board_foot_dbh = 1,
                    scribner = 'table')
## Translate the complete rule record
translated <- products_from_nvel_rules(x = rules)
product min_sed min_length max_length scale_rule
nvel_primary 6 8 40 scribner_decimal_c_whole_40
nvel_secondary 4 8 40 scribner_decimal_c_whole_40

Translated products retain expanded source measurement fields. The returned list also contains stump_ht, utilization_height, and model_aux. The translated height cap adds stump to merchantable_length. Both translated products retain board-foot measurement, including the product accepting pulp restrictions.
